tweets: Chennakeshava Temple, Belur — begun in 1117 CE by the Hoysaḻa king Viṣṇuvardhana on the banks of the Yagachi river. Carved in soft chloritic schist that hardens with age, it took some 103 years and three generations of Hoysaḻa rule to finish.

On the jagati platform circling the shrine, friezes of elephants, horsemen and warriors; above, bracket figures include the celebrated Darpaṇa Sundari, a woman gazing into her mirror. Follow @yddoseOfHistory for your daily dose of history.
